about: lib/product-pricing.js priceProduct and labour ONCE per product (Turki, Nov 19; data model: Mac Figma p.18). A product with its own `rates` costs each part's material, wear and power by its own print time, and the labour, (prep + post) × rate × (1 + failure/100), once. `labourPerPart: true` puts labour back in every part. A product with NO `rates` (every product saved before this) costs exactly as before. One part here: 100 g of 90/1000 g filament (9.00), 2 h at wear 0.75 (1.50) and 150 W × 0.18 (0.054), +10% failure = 11.6094 without labour; labour 0.75 h × 90 × 1.1 = 74.25. The Mac and the phone run this file.

cases.why: a single item: the catalogue costs it exactly as the calculator does (11.61 + 74.25)
labourPerPart: the explicit override puts labour back in every part: 15 × 85.86
LEGACY: a product with no rates (6 parts carrying their own) costs exactly as before: 6 × 85.86, no silent re-price
a part's own rate wins over the product's: one part at 120 W instead of 150 changes only its power
